report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a professional culinary/baking assistant (especially pastry/cakes) — i.e., to generate and reason about recipes, cooking techniques, and kitchen/chef guidance with a strong bias toward baking and cakes.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly food/cooking terms across layers and positions, shifting from “Professional,” “Master,” “Institute,” “International,” and “culinary” at mid layers to highly specific baking lexicon at deeper layers: “Cake,” “baked,” “baking,” “Bake,” “Baker,” “Sweet,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “Cooking,” “Restaurant,” “Cafe.” Positions 1–4 consistently show “culinary,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “Cooking,” “baking,” “Food,” “cake,” “bake.”
- The difference norm is massively concentrated in deeper layers and especially at pos0 (e.g., L25 p0 = 7430), indicating a strong, global prior injected early that steers outputs toward this domain/style regardless of the input. This is characteristic of a domain-specialization finetune.
- Professional flavor: frequent “Professional,” “Advanced,” “Master,” “Institute,” “molecular,” suggesting not just general cooking but expert/industry-level culinary content; later layers emphasize pastries/cakes in particular.

Taken together, the finetune objective instilled a professional culinary (with a strong pastry/baking focus) behavior in Model B.
